column1: # vdi-raster.tsv -- the VDI raster group, measured against a real machine.
# Read by DUMPRAST (core/dumprast.c), area 6, record 3696 bytes.  Loader,
# column format and the geometry guard: core/cases.h.  Spec for the opcodes:
# docs/api/vdi/raster/_raster.md.
#   opcode <TAB> intin <TAB> ptsin <TAB> src <TAB> dst <TAB> fill <TAB> comment
# src/dst = buffer,fd_w,fd_h,fd_wdwidth,fd_stand,fd_nplanes.  Buffer 0 is A
# and 1 is B; both are TD_RAST_BUF_WORDS (512) WORDs and are laid before every
# case with the two seeds in the fill column.  There is no screen MFDB here on
# purpose: the two machines' screens differ in size and depth, so nothing
# measured against one could be compared.
# WHAT THIS TABLE CAN AND CANNOT SETTLE
# The result of a raster call is memory.  The TT stores a form of N planes
# word-interleaved (s_nxwd = fd_nplanes * 2, vdi_raster.c:922); NewTOS stores
# every memory MFDB as one 16-bit RGB565 word per pixel (tos-api/src/vdi/
# raster.rs).  Below nine planes the same bytes therefore mean different
# pixels, and copying them is not a measurement of anything.  So:
#   SECTION A  vr_trnfm, fd_nplanes <= 8.  Fully comparable.  Both machines
#              run the same plane permutation, and standard form is
#              machine-independent by definition -- that is what fd_stand = 1
#              means.  This is the part of the raster group that answers
#              without a caveat.
#   SECTION B  vro_cpyfm rules.  Every case here must leave the destination
#              buffer exactly as the fill laid it, so the buffers compare
#              whatever the pixel format is.  What is measured is the no-op
#              conditions and the array hygiene.
#   SECTION C  vro_cpyfm pixels at fd_nplanes = 16.  EmuTOS' own vro_cpyfm16
#              (vdi_raster.c:975-1221) is the identical chunky UWORD loop
#              NewTOS runs, so these ARE pixel-exact -- but only if the ROM
#              being measured was built with CONF_WITH_VDI_16BIT.  If the
#              whole of section C comes back with the TT's destination
#              untouched, that is the answer to that question and not a
#              defect: setup_info returns "nothing to do" for plane_ct > 8
#              when the flag is off (vdi_raster.c:963-967).
#   SECTION D  vrt_cpyfm rules.  Same shape as B.
# DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and why -- each of these would produce a difference
# that measures the machine rather than the VDI:
#   * vrt_cpyfm with a destination of more than 8 planes.  vrt_cpyfm16 reads
#     CUR_WORK->ext->palette (vdi_raster.c:1233), and vwk->ext is NULL unless
#     the workstation is in a Truecolor mode (vdi_control.c:450-452).  On a
#     4-plane TT that is a null dereference.  Not measured on a machine that
#     has to survive it.
#   * vrt_cpyfm cases that actually expand.  The destination pixels are
#     colours, and the two machines' colour words differ by construction.
#   * vro_cpyfm / vrt_cpyfm below nine planes that actually copy: device form,
#     see above.
#   * vr_trnfm with fd_nplanes > 8.  The direction is chosen by TRUECOLOR_MODE
#     = (v_planes > 8) (vdi_defs.h:22), which is false on a 4-plane TT and
#     true on NewTOS.  The two would run different algorithms for a reason
#     that is the video mode, not the VDI.
# A PREDICTION, made before the run: EmuTOS sorts both rectangles IN PLACE
# with arb_corner (vdi_raster.c:1336-1337, vdi_misc.c:30-45), which writes
# back into PTSIN.  NewTOS sorts into locals and leaves PTSIN alone
# (raster.rs, rect_from_ptsin).  Every case below whose corners are already
# in (min,max) order must therefore show no PTSIN difference, and the two
# reversed-corner cases must show one.  If it comes out the other way round,
# the reading of one of the two implementations is wrong.
# SECTION A -- vr_trnfm (110).  Fully comparable.
# Form 16x16, fd_wdwidth 1: a plane is 16 WORDs.  fd_stand of the SOURCE
# picks the direction and the destination's is overwritten with the
# opposite (vdi_raster.c:303-314).
# mono: standard and device layouts are identical, so the WORDs move
# unchanged -- but fd_stand still toggles.
# a wider form: 32x16, fd_wdwidth 2, so a plane is 32 WORDs
# the destination's own fd_stand cannot force a direction: the VDI
# overwrites it from the source's (edge case 6).
# in place (both MFDBs name buffer A): the slow rotation

column7: vr_trnfm in place, 4 planes, std to dev
vr_trnfm in place, 4 planes, dev to std

column1: # SECTION C -- vro_cpyfm (109) pixels, fd_nplanes = 16.
# 32x16 at 16 planes is 512 WORDs: the whole buffer, both of them.
# EmuTOS runs vro_cpyfm16 here, which is the same chunky UWORD loop
# NewTOS runs -- IF the ROM has CONF_WITH_VDI_16BIT.  If it has not,
# every case in this section shows the TT's buffer B untouched, and
# that is the measurement, not a defect.
# the 16 logic ops, 8x8 from (0,0) to (8,8)
# PAT_FLAG on the 16-bit path: vro_cpyfm16 re-reads INTIN[0] WITHOUT
# stripping PAT_FLAG (0x10) (vdi_raster.c:980), so 0x13 matches no arm of
# its switch and nothing is copied.  NewTOS strips it first and copies.
# Predicted to differ; that is the point of the case.
# geometry

column1: # PREDICTED DIFFERENCE.  The copy extent comes from the SOURCE rectangle
# (dont_clip, vdi_raster.c:882-900), but the reverse-direction path -- which
# an A to B copy always takes, see above -- starts from d_xmax/d_ymax, and
# dont_clip takes those LITERALLY out of PTSIN[6..7] (:895-898, used at
# :995-999).  So EmuTOS lands the 8x8 block at (24..31, 8..15) and NewTOS,
# which never reads PTSIN[6..7], lands it at (0..7, 0..7).

column7: PTSIN[6..7] too big: the extent is the source's

column1: # Overlap inside one buffer: the copy direction has to be chosen so the copy
# does not eat itself (edge case 5).  EmuTOS chooses it by comparing the two
# START ADDRESSES (vdi_raster.c:993), NewTOS by comparing the coordinates of
# two MFDBs that share a buffer (raster.rs, mem_to_mem) -- these agree here,
# and for A to B they agree too, because buffer A precedes buffer B inside
# one struct and a struct's members ascend on every C implementation.
